name: Projection-Induced Orientation Dynamics Registry

core_definition.canonical_statement: Projection-induced orientation dynamics describe how local orientation consistency is retained, deformed, bifurcated, or lost within projection-derived persistence structures.
core_definition.non_primitive_rule: Orientation behavior remains projection-derived and must trace to an indivisible ⇔R source relation.

orientation_states.name: orientation_consistent
orientation_states.definition: Projected persistence structure retains stable local orientation alignment.

orientation_states.name: orientation_deforming
orientation_states.definition: Projected persistence structure changes orientation while preserving bounded coherence.

orientation_states.name: orientation_bifurcating
orientation_states.definition: Projected orientation splits into multiple admissible local orientation pathways.

orientation_states.name: orientation_overcompressed
orientation_states.definition: Projected orientation becomes too constrained to preserve stable continuation readability.

orientation_states.name: orientation_dissolving
orientation_states.definition: Projected orientation loses enough coherence that the persistence structure cannot retain local orientation identity.

transition_conditions.condition: local admissibility gradient changes while source traceability remains preserved
multiple orientation-compatible continuation channels become locally admissible
orientation constraints exceed bounded flexibility threshold
orientation coherence fails below local persistence threshold

governance_rules.rule: Orientation dynamics must declare source_relation and projection_depth.
Orientation consistency does not imply primitive orientation ontology.
Orientation bifurcation does not imply physical branching.
Orientation overcompression must be treated as projection failure risk, not source-relation failure.
Orientation dynamics cannot be used as evidence for physical spacetime, quantum state, or GR-like derivation.

allowed_uses: Tracking orientation consistency inside projection-induced persistence structures.
Classifying orientation deformation and bifurcation under admissibility constraints.
Linking orientation dynamics to projection persistence dynamics without primitive promotion.
forbidden_uses: Treating orientation bifurcation as physical branching.
Using projected orientation as proof of physical geometry.
Using orientation dynamics to claim QM/GR derivation.
